messages:
jordan (customer): Hey, hitting spikes in p95/p99 for streaming responses since yesterday afternoon. TTFB looks fine but total time is way up for some sessions. It’s impacting user chat experience.

jordan (customer): We use streaming SSE to render tokens client-side. Non-streaming calls (sync) have lower total latency for the same prompt set, ironically.

sara (support): Sorry you're seeing this, @jordan. Can you share a sample request + headers and an example of the p95/p99 numbers you’re observing? Also which model + region?

jordan (customer): Sure — model `redwood-1.0-large` in us-west-2. p95 increased from ~320ms to 1.8s; p99 from ~650ms to 4.2s. TTFB (first byte) stays ~120ms.

jordan (customer): Repro curl:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0-large","prompt":"translate: hello","stream":true}' \\ 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate/stream
```

jordan (customer): We already tried reducing client buffer sizes; still see big tail latencies.

sara (support): Thanks. Opening a triage with eng runtime. @michael, can you take a look? Looks like streaming chunk delivery / flush timing causing total-time regression even though server starts sending.

michael (eng-runtime): Noted. A few quick theories: 1) chunk coalescing / flush heuristic changed in runtime recently, 2) KV cache pressure causing intermittent stalls during token generation, 3) autoscaler packing causing bursts and queueing.

michael (eng-runtime): Can you capture one full session with headers + chunk boundaries? If you can share raw SSE frames (or browser devtools network HAR) that shows gap between first and subsequent chunks that’d help.

jordan (customer): Pasted a trimmed HAR into a Gist (link): https://gist.github.com/jordan/abc123 — large gaps between chunk 1 and chunk 2 (~1.6s).

dave (sre): I pulled infra metrics around that timestamp range — noted increased GPU reorder and a spike in batching queues at the same minute. Also saw a transient 5–10s noise in the model process logs on one host.

olivia (prod-eng): Was there any rolling deploy or runtime config change yesterday? @deploy-bot can you confirm deploys to the serving pool?

deploy-bot: deploy started by ops@redwood at 2026-03-14T15:20:03Z; rollout=canary->all; config change: batching.flush_interval_ms from 20 -> 50 (canary).

michael (eng-runtime): Aha — flush_interval_ms bumped to 50ms in canary — that would increase coalescing. Usually that affects TTFB minimally but can increase chunk delay patterns for short responses. However your TTFB was unchanged so the bigger delays imply additional queuing or background GC.

michael (eng-runtime): Two parallel things to check: 1) Are requests hitting canary nodes with the new flush interval? 2) Is batching causing a bigger batch at token N leading to pause while batch finishes building?

jordan (customer): How do we force traffic off the canary? Users are impacted.

sara (support): We can route your account to stable pool temporarily. Want me to flip that?

jordan (customer): Please do. Also, any short-term workarounds we can apply client-side?

michael (eng-runtime): Short-term options: 1) Toggle `stream=false` (non-streaming) — will avoid chunking but increases time-to-first-complete; you already said sync was faster for you, so this is viable. 2) Add an explicit low-level keepalive/frame request — not ideal. 3) We can route to stable infra which has flush_interval_ms=20.

dave (sre): I've scheduled a routing override for account_id=acct_98765 to force stable pool; should take effect in ~2 minutes. Will monitor p95/p99.

michael (eng-runtime): For root cause we need to correlate these things: flush interval change + observed batching queue spike + that one host process noise. Please capture full server-side token emission logs with `X-Trace-Id` from a failing session. That will show the exact timing of token enqueue vs network flush.

jordan (customer): I can provide X-Trace-Id. After you route us back to stable, I'll run a controlled test and paste traces.

olivia (prod-eng): Long-term mitigation items for our backlog:
- revert or refine the canary flush_interval change (config granular by workload).
- add adaptive flush heuristics that prioritize low-latency short responses (detect short prompt and lower coalescing).
- add streaming-specific SLOs and automated rollback trigger when p99 for streaming increases by >50%.

michael (eng-runtime): Also adding an A/B test: for streaming requests under 64 tokens, set flush_interval=10ms and max_coalesce_tokens=4. That should reduce chunk gaps.

sara (support): Update: routing override complete, @jordan — please confirm if you see improvements.

jordan (customer): Confirmed — after routing to stable, p95 down to ~340ms, p99 ~700ms. Huge improvement, thanks.

jordan (customer): I ran a repro and attached trace id TRACE-20260314-9fd2. HAR shows steady ~20–40ms inter-chunk intervals now.

michael (eng-runtime): Got the trace. Server logs show earlier noise on host gpu-host-17 where the runtime process did a memory compaction coinciding with the observed 1.6s gap — that matches dave’s infra spike. The canary config made the pause worse for short-response streams because coalescing held tokens instead of flushing.

michael (eng-runtime): Root cause = combination of canary flush_interval increase + transient process stall on a host. Not a single bug but config + infra compounding.

olivia (prod-eng): Action items and owners:
- michael: roll a fix to reduce canary flush_interval for short streams + add adaptive heuristic (P0 for short-chat UX).
- dave: investigate host-level memory compaction events and GC settings on gpu-host-17 (followup with infra team).
- sara: keep routing override until rollout verified.
- jordan: verify no more regressions and share any further traces.

sara (support): We'll keep this thread updated. Thanks for the quick repro @jordan and for the infra catch @dave. :thumbsup:

michael (eng-runtime): Temp mitigation we’ll push in the next 2 hours: set canary flush_interval back to 20ms for streaming endpoints and enable a flag `streaming.adaptive_flush=true` (gradual rollout).

dave (sre): For tracking, I'll create incident-INC-2026-032 to follow infra remediation.

jordan (customer): Appreciated. Happy to help verify any fixes.

sara (support): Closing loop: p95/p99 returned to expected after routing to stable. Keeping this open until adaptive flush is validated. Will update when deployment starts.

michael (eng-runtime): Deployment started at 2026-03-14T18:05:00Z for adaptive flush flag (partial rollout). Monitoring p99 on streaming; will roll back if exceeds threshold.

sara (support): Marking this thread as ongoing; will update when all actions complete.

jordan (customer): Thanks everyone.
